purpose: Implements a Remove Unused CSS feature with a PHP-based purge engine that parses HTML per page, strips unused CSS rules, and caches purged CSS per URL in the existing cache directory structure. Integrates with the output buffer pipeline, REST API, cron, and admin UI.
riskRationale: Three critical issues: (1) CDN rewriting runs before used-CSS so regex-based <link> removal uses non-CDN URLs and silently fails when CDN is enabled — both full original CSS and used-CSS load simultaneously, negating the performance benefit. (2) MinifyCSS similarly rewrites href to minified URLs before used-CSS, causing the same silent failure. (3) Race condition in used-CSS file writes can produce corrupted output under concurrent requests.

text: The feature is architecturally sound, following existing plugin patterns well with a comprehensive safelist, WP_HTML_Tag_Processor integration, and clean UI integration. However, three critical pipeline-ordering bugs and a race condition must be resolved before merging. The selector-matching and CSS parsing logic has several correctness gaps that reduce effectiveness but are acceptable for a v1 with documented limitations.

reasoning: Three critical issues (CDN ordering, minifyCSS ordering, race condition in save_used_css) and important performance regression (no cache-read-before-generate in process_buffer) must be fixed before merging. All fixes are straightforward and safe for automated application.

message: Built-in safelist is comprehensive and conservative — covers admin bar, WooCommerce, WordPress core, JS prefixes, @font-face, @keyframes, and common UI states. Good defensive design.
CSS parser properly handles nested @media/@supports blocks with brace-depth tracking, one of the harder parts of lightweight CSS parsing.

process_buffer() has a proper guard for background regeneration requests (X-WPPO-Used-CSS header) preventing infinite loops, and falls back to the original buffer on filesystem write failure. Graceful degradation.
Used-CSS integration follows the same buffer pipeline pattern as CDN rewriting and image optimisation — consistent architecture and easy to locate.
The used_css_regenerate endpoint correctly supports both single-post and full background queue modes, matching the existing Action Scheduler pattern.
4 well-written tests cover the used-CSS UI: rendering the switch, toggling shows safelist/button, submit payload inclusion, and regenerate button API call.
The withNotification abstraction cleanly reduces code duplication across handleSubmit, handleRegenerateCss, and handleRegenerateUsedCSS.
used_css_cron() follows existing patterns with transient-based locking and proper try/finally cleanup — consistent with img_convert_cron and database_cleanup_cron.

CDN rewriting runs BEFORE used-CSS in the buffer pipeline. The used-CSS process_buffer removes <link> tags by matching original src URLs from $wp_styles->registered, but maybe_apply_cdn() has already rewritten all href values to CDN URLs. The regex can't match, so original <link> tags remain alongside the injected used-CSS <link> — both full original CSS and purged CSS load simultaneously, negating the performance benefit.
suggestion: Move maybe_apply_used_css() before maybe_apply_cdn() in process_buffer_only() so the regex-based <link> removal sees original (non-CDN) URLs.

message: Race condition in save_used_css(): multiple concurrent requests for the same page URL all generate purged CSS and call save_used_css() concurrently. The file is written via put_contents() without any advisory locking or atomic write pattern. Concurrent writes can produce truncated or interleaved CSS content.
suggestion: Use an atomic write pattern: write to a temporary file, then rename/move to the final path.

message: When minifyCSS is also enabled, minify_css() in class-main.php rewrites <link> hrefs to minified CSS file URLs before process_buffer() runs. The regex tries to match against the original $wp_styles->registered[$handle]->src, which no longer exists in the HTML. The match silently fails, so original <link> tags remain alongside the injected used-CSS link — duplicating CSS instead of reducing it.
suggestion: After fetching CSS assets, compute the minified URL for each handle and include those URLs in the link-removal regex. Alternatively, restructure the buffer pipeline so used-CSS runs before minification.

message: process_buffer() runs the full CSS parse, purge, and filesystem-write pipeline on every single page load without checking for a cached used-css.css file first. Every visitor pays the cost of parsing potentially hundreds of KB of CSS, extracting selectors from the full HTML, and writing a file — a significant performance regression.
suggestion: Check if a cached used-css.css exists and is newer than its source CSS files before running generation. If cached, inject the existing file URL and return early.

message: matches_simple_selector() uses regex `::?[a-z\-]+(?:\([^()]*\))?` to strip pseudo-classes/pseudo-elements. The `[^()]*` does not handle nested parentheses — selectors like `:not(.a:not(.b))` or `:is(.class1, :where(.class2))` leave unmatched `)`, causing false negatives (rules incorrectly removed).
suggestion: Replace the regex with a character-by-character parser that tracks parenthesis depth, similar to how split_selectors() handles comma nesting.

message: extract_selectors() only captures `type`, `rel`, `role`, `href`, `src`, and `data-` attribute prefixes. Common attribute selectors like `[aria-hidden]`, `[aria-label]`, `[target]`, `[tabindex]`, or `[disabled]` are not tracked in $used['attrs'], so CSS rules using these attribute selectors will be incorrectly removed (false negatives).
suggestion: Expand attribute tracking to cover common global HTML attributes, or iterate all attributes returned by WP_HTML_Tag_Processor::get_attribute() instead of using a hardcoded list.

message: fetch_css_content_static() (line 971) and fetch_css_content() (line 1028) are near-identical duplicates — same logic, same fallback chain. The only difference is static vs instance method, violating DRY.
suggestion: Make the instance method call the static one, or refactor to a single private static method.

message: is_selector_used() treats descendant/child combinators as independent checks — for `.sidebar .widget`, it returns true if EITHER `.sidebar` OR `.widget` exists anywhere in the HTML. This makes purging far more conservative than a true PurgeCSS, keeping rules like `body.admin-bar .menu-item-123` anytime any individual class is present. The claimed 30-80% reduction is unachievable with this strategy.
suggestion: Document this design trade-off explicitly in the method docblock and plugin UI. For a v1 this conservative approach is acceptable (avoids false positives), but performance claims should be tempered.

message: The CSS comment-stripping regex `preg_replace('/\/\*.*?\*\//s', '', $css)` does not handle string contents — if a CSS declaration contains `content: "/* not a comment */"`, the string content between `/*` and `*/` would be stripped, breaking the rule.
suggestion: Use a more robust comment-stripping approach that respects string boundaries (e.g., tokenize CSS). For a v1, add a docblock noting this limitation.

message: parse_css_block_rules() is identical in structure to the main rule-parsing section of parse_css() but operates on flat blocks only — it doesn't handle nested @-rules inside @media/@supports. Nested @-rules would be parsed incorrectly.
suggestion: Reuse parse_css() recursively for block content instead of maintaining a separate flat parser.

message: delete_all_used_css() only iterates 2 directory levels deep (domain/ and domain/path/). If the cache structure evolves to support deeper URL nesting, some used-css.css files would not be deleted.
suggestion: Use RecursiveDirectoryIterator to find all used-css.css files under the cache root recursively.

message: The filename 'used-css.css' is hardcoded as a string literal at multiple locations. Should be a class constant for maintainability.
suggestion: Define `const USED_CSS_FILENAME = 'used-css.css';` and reference it consistently.

message: The setTimeout to clear notification after 3 seconds in withNotification()'s finally block creates a stale timeout hazard — if the user re-submits within 3 seconds, the old timeout fires and clears the new notification.
suggestion: Store the timeout ID in a ref and clear it at the top of withNotification before setting a new one.

message: regenerate_all() queues all background jobs in a synchronous loop using as_enqueue_async_action() for each post in batches of 200. On a site with 50,000+ published posts, this could cause memory exhaustion.
suggestion: Use Action Scheduler's group-based scheduling with a single action that processes a batch, similar to the preload cron's offset-based approach in class-cron.php.

message: The test 'submit includes removeUnusedCSS and excludeUnusedCSS in settings payload' passes settings via the options prop but never tests the actual form flow (toggle -> type -> submit). It only tests that options are forwarded on submit.
suggestion: Add a test that verifies the end-to-end form interaction for the new fields, not just prop forwarding.

message: handleRegenerateUsedCSS() and handleSubmit() call withNotification() without awaiting it, creating a floating promise that could trigger a React state-update-on-unmounted-component warning.
suggestion: Return the promise from withNotification and await it in callers.
